sources.title: LangGraph: Add and manage memory (checkpointers, trim, delete, summarize, long-term store)
sources.summary: Canonical LangGraph reference for short-term memory via checkpointers keyed by thread_id (InMemorySaver/PostgresSaver/Redis/Mongo), plus three in-graph context controls: trim_messages with count_tokens_approximately, RemoveMessage/REMOVE_ALL_MESSAGES deletion, and a SummarizationNode that maintains a RunningSummary. Long-term memory lives in a separate Store (InMemoryStore/PostgresStore) with embedding-based semantic search accessed via runtime.store.

sources.title: LangMem Short-Term Memory API (SummarizationNode, RunningSummary)
sources.summary: API reference for LangMem's short-term memory utilities that LangGraph imports: summarize_messages and SummarizationNode compress older turns into a RunningSummary once a max_tokens budget is exceeded, keeping recent messages verbatim and passing the summary forward.

sources.title: LlamaIndex: Memory (token budgets + StaticMemoryBlock / FactExtractionMemoryBlock / VectorMemoryBlock)
sources.summary: LlamaIndex's Memory class enforces a token_limit (default 30k) split by chat_history_token_ratio (0.7); when short-term exceeds its share, token_flush_size (3k) tokens are flushed into long-term memory blocks. Three block types (static, LLM fact-extraction with max_facts, vector retrieval with similarity_top_k) are injected into the system or user message by insert_method, and each carries a priority (0 = never evicted) that governs truncation order; backing store is SQLite by default or any async SQL URI.

sources.title: Letta: Memory blocks (core memory)
sources.summary: Memory blocks are labeled, size-limited XML sections pinned into the agent's context window and always visible without retrieval. Agents edit them with built-in tools (memory_replace, memory_insert, memory_rethink); blocks can be read-only, and multiple agents can attach to the same block so updates propagate immediately.

sources.title: Letta: Archival memory
sources.summary: Describes the MemGPT-derived hierarchy: core memory (in-context, like RAM) versus archival and recall memory (out-of-context, like disk). Agents page data between tiers with tool calls, creating the illusion of unbounded memory within a fixed context; recall memory is the automatically persisted full message history that can be searched.

sources.title: Letta: Sleep-time agents
sources.summary: Sleep-time agents share a primary agent's memory blocks but run asynchronously in the background, reading conversation history and rewriting the blocks with 'learned context'. This decouples memory management from the response path, improving latency and memory quality versus the original single-agent MemGPT design.

sources.title: Mem0 Platform Overview (universal memory layer)
sources.summary: Mem0 sits between the app and the LLM, using LLM-powered fact extraction to store and update user preferences and conversational facts, then retrieving them by semantic (and optionally graph) search so only relevant memories are injected per turn. Available as hosted Platform or self-hosted OSS.

sources.title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory
sources.summary: Introduces Graphiti, a temporally-aware knowledge graph engine that synthesizes unstructured conversation and structured business data while preserving historical relationships, and reports gains over MemGPT on DMR and on the LongMemEval benchmark.

sources.title: What Is a Temporal Knowledge Graph? (Zep / Graphiti)
sources.summary: Zep's explainer for its memory model: every fact carries when it became true, when it stopped being true, and its source episode. Bi-temporal edges and automatic fact invalidation let agents retrieve what was true at a point in time instead of stuffing transcripts into context.
sources.popularity_signal: Page cites 20,000+ GitHub stars for Graphiti; current getzep/graphiti 30,134 stars

sources.title: cognee: open-source AI memory platform (graph-vector hybrid)
sources.summary: Cognee gives agents persistent long-term memory by ingesting data into a self-hosted knowledge graph with a unified graph, vector, and relational storage layer, then exposing search over it so agents retrieve structure-aware context rather than raw chunks.

sources.title: OpenAI Agents SDK: Sessions
sources.summary: Session protocol (get_items/add_items/pop_item/clear_session) with backends from SQLiteSession to SQLAlchemy, Redis, MongoDB, Dapr and OpenAIConversationsSession. Context is controlled via SessionSettings(limit=N), a session_input_callback that rewrites history before each model call, OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession for automatic Responses-API compaction (with manual run_compaction), and EncryptedSession wrappers.

sources.title: OpenAI Cookbook: Context Engineering - Short-Term Memory Management with Sessions
sources.summary: Walks through implementing custom Session classes for the Agents SDK that either trim (keep last N turns; deterministic, zero added latency, verbatim recent tool results) or summarize older turns, and discusses the trade-offs between the two approaches.

sources.title: Claude Platform: Context editing (clear_tool_uses, clear_thinking)
sources.summary: Server-side context_management edits under beta header context-management-2025-06-27: clear_tool_uses_20250919 replaces old tool results once a trigger (default 100k input tokens) fires, keeping the last N pairs (default 3) with clear_at_least, exclude_tools and clear_tool_inputs knobs; clear_thinking_20251015 prunes thinking blocks by keep thinking_turns. Documents cache-invalidation behaviour, count_tokens support, and notes a deprecated SDK-side compaction_control alternative.
sources.popularity_signal: anthropics/claude-code 142,118 GitHub stars (org); widely referenced by agent frameworks

sources.title: Claude Platform: Memory tool
sources.summary: Client-implemented file memory tool (view/create/str_replace/insert/delete/rename under /memories) that lets Claude persist notes across conversations. Pairs with context editing: when the clearing threshold approaches, Claude is warned so it can write tool results to memory before they are cleared.

sources.title: Claude Cookbook: Context engineering - memory, compaction, and tool clearing
sources.summary: Hands-on notebook combining the memory tool, context editing, and summarization-based compaction in one agent loop, showing how to keep long tool-heavy sessions within budget while preserving state in memory files.

sources.title: Claude Code: Explore the context window (interactive)
sources.summary: Interactive simulation of how Claude Code's 200k window fills: system prompt, auto memory (first 200 lines/25KB of MEMORY.md), CLAUDE.md files, deferred MCP tool schemas (loaded on demand via tool search; ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH), skill index, then file reads which dominate usage. Shows subagents working in a separate window and returning only a summary, and /compact replacing the conversation with a structured summary after which system prompt, CLAUDE.md, memory and MCP tools reload automatically (the skill listing is the exception).

sources.title: Claude Agent SDK: Subagents in the SDK
sources.summary: Subagents are separate agent instances with their own system prompt, context window, tool list and permission mode, spawned to isolate context, run analyses in parallel, and keep large intermediate output out of the parent; the SDK also handles automatic compaction near the limit and re-reads CLAUDE.md after compaction.

sources.title: Using Claude Code: session management and 1M context
sources.summary: Anthropic's guidance on long Claude Code sessions: with a 1M window there is more room to /compact proactively with a description of what to keep, or to delegate to subagents that get a clean context and return only their result; recommends subagents when a chunk of work will produce lots of intermediate output you will not need again.

sources.title: Google ADK: Memory (MemoryService, Vertex AI Memory Bank)
sources.summary: ADK splits Session (event log + State) from MemoryService; add_session_to_memory ingests completed sessions and VertexAiMemoryBankService uses an LLM to extract and consolidate salient facts, which agents later fetch with search_memory / load_memory tools, so old details are recalled without loading old transcripts into the window.

sources.title: Semantic Kernel: Creating and managing a chat history object (Chat History Reduction)
sources.summary: Defines IChatHistoryReducer (.NET) and ChatHistoryReducer (Python) with two built-ins: ChatHistoryTruncationReducer drops oldest messages beyond target_count, ChatHistorySummarizationReducer summarizes the removed messages back into one message; threshold_count buffers so function call/result pairs are not split, system messages are always kept, and Python's auto_reduce applies reduction on add_message_async. Java unsupported.

sources.title: AutoGen: Model Context (BufferedChatCompletionContext and friends)
sources.summary: AutoGen agents take a model_context object that decides which stored messages are sent to the model; BufferedChatCompletionContext keeps only the most recent buffer_size messages (MRU), with token-limited and head-and-tail variants, letting developers bound context without changing agent logic.

sources.title: CrewAI: Memory (unified Memory with scoped recall)
sources.summary: CrewAI replaced its separate short-term/long-term/entity memories with one Memory class: on save an LLM infers scope (filesystem-like paths such as /project/alpha), categories and importance; recall ranks by semantic_weight*similarity + recency_weight*decay + importance_weight*importance with adaptive depth. Crews auto-extract atomic facts after each task and inject relevant memories before the next; memory=True enables defaults, LanceDB is the default backend, and a StorageBackend protocol allows custom stores.

sources.title: Pydantic AI: Messages and chat history (history processors)
sources.summary: Agent(history_processors=[...]) runs functions over the message list before each model call to prune, summarize or rewrite history; processors can take RunContext to act on current token usage, e.g. summarize the oldest messages with a cheaper model when usage is high. Docs warn that tool calls and returns must stay paired after summarization.

sources.title: Vercel AI SDK: pruneMessages
sources.summary: pruneMessages(ModelMessage[]) strips reasoning ('all' | 'before-last-message' | 'none'), tool call/result/approval parts ('all' | 'before-last-message' | 'before-last-N-messages' | per-tool arrays) and empty messages before a model call, typically inside a per-step prepare hook to cap context growth in tool loops.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol specification (2025-06-18): Resources
sources.summary: Specifies how MCP servers expose read-only, URI-addressed resources (files, schemas, logs) that the host application, not the model, chooses to pull into context, with list/read/subscribe operations; distinguishes application-driven resources from model-invoked tools so context loading stays deliberate.
sources.popularity_signal: modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol 9,007 GitHub stars; adopted by Claude, OpenAI, Google SDKs

sources.title: Aider: Building a better repository map with tree-sitter
sources.summary: Foundational write-up of Aider's repo map: tree-sitter tags.scm queries extract definitions and references per file, a dependency graph is ranked (PageRank-style) for relevance to the current chat, and a token-budgeted summary of the most important symbols is sent instead of whole files so the LLM can navigate large repos.
sources.popularity_signal: Aider-AI/aider 48,354 GitHub stars; pattern copied by many tools (RepoMapper, agentpatterns.ai)

sources.title: Cline's Context Window Explained: Maximize Performance, Minimize Cost
sources.summary: Explains Cline's context budget, why performance degrades around 70-80% fill, and its mitigations: a visual context progress bar, @file/@url mentions for precise context, and an automated handoff via the new_task tool driven by .clinerules (e.g. 'if context exceeds 50%, carry over X') so a fresh task starts with a curated summary.

sources.title: DSPy: Managing Conversation History (dspy.History)
techniques: explicit history as typed input field
sources.summary: DSPy deliberately does not manage conversation history inside modules; dspy.History is a typed input field (messages: list[dict]) that adapters format into the prompt, leaving truncation/summarization to the program author so history can be optimized like any other signature input.
